I went through some of the matters that I submit the Court needs to consider so far as the words "in part" are concerned, so far as the words "to destroy" are concerned and they simply aren't made out notwithstanding what Mr. Tieger has said, and even under a -- the test as adopted in the Rule 98 bis Milosevic decision, which both parties have agreed is the right test, even under that test, one can't just pluck a few facts out of the air and say well, based on those there is a sufficiency of evidence in relation to what amounts to, to state the obvious, an extremely serious charge. That's how I put it in response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Finally, perhaps it's unnecessary to establish, Mr. Tieger, but Mr. Josse this morning started with a kind of a general statement that an acquittal on all counts, on all charges, would be appropriate at this moment and he told us that he discussed the matter with Mr. Krajisnik. I take it of course where the Prosecution responded mainly on the basis of the specific issues that the general line is that you would reject such a suggestion at all because you didn't address the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, the Court is quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: What Mr. Tieger also hasn't addressed - and I make no complaint about it, I just observe it was -- and it may be because it was something I didn't discuss with him as fully as I might otherwise have done - which was my very last point, which was that looking at the way Judge Agius put it in the Oric discussion, he was suggesting that regardless of what the parties were saying, a full, reasoned decision is required on sufficiency of evidence at this stage, and I note Mr. Tieger hasn't addressed that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me note preliminarily that that was -- I haven't focussed in particular on that submission because I don't think it was the subject of discussions before. I will say I don't see anything in Rule 98 bis that requires the Court to proprio motu do the same thing that used to be done by the parties with respect to 98 bis. I'm sure that's not the intention of 98 bis. It is an oral decision after hearing the submissions. I take on board Judge Agius's comments that Rule 98 bis is no longer specifically party-driven as opposed to perhaps imposing a different kind of burden on the Court. I recall some comment by Judge Liu in an earlier case that if submissions were not made by the parties then the Court had no further responsibility. That may or may not be the case under 98 bis now but I don't think that rises to the level of some highly detailed analysis of all the evidence in the case, if that's what was being suggested. I think if it's clear to the Court that one of the counts cannot stand under the standards articulated earlier, that's another story and a reasoned decision must follow. And -- but it strikes me that the suggestion, if I heard that properly, that the Court is obliged to engage in roughly the same kind of an exhaustive review of the evidence that once produced essentially two trials in these cases is misplaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Josse, I take it that there is some relation between the details in which the Chamber should enter under the old or the new Rule - whether it's just counts or also part of a count, 1 A and B, genocide against one group, genocide against another group, whether it's 18 victims or 12 victims just referring to one of my earlier examples - I take it that the parties would understand that going through all the -- I would say the little details as in practice was done before is not something that becomes the apparent duty of the Chamber under the new Rule, which is of course something totally different from whether a reasoned decision has to be given. And if I do understand you well, if, for example, you might have missed an important matter on Count 7 there would have been no evidence whatever being presented, that you would expect the Chamber to give a reasoned decision why an acquittal on Count 7 then had to be given. That's -- you expect us not to just give a yes or no but to give some other reasons in whatever detail that would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: My submission is really a hybrid one inasmuch as I recognise that under the new Rule, once the Chamber certainly does not need to go through schedule line by line. Indeed probably doesn't need to go through the schedule at all. But what I understood Judge Agius to be saying was what the Chamber does have to do is go through the indictment count by count and be satisfied in its own mind that the Prosecution have made out a case, a case for the accused to answer, on each count and then give reasons as to why there is a case in relation to each count dealing with the generality of the count rather than the specificity of it. That's what I understood Judge Agius to be saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. If the parties have made all their submissions, since we have no further questions -- yes, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, just before the Court was to adjourn, I wanted to either raise or foreshadow an unrelated issue, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But before I give you an opportunity to do so, I want to ask one question. I do understand that at least for two municipalities the Prosecution accepts that there is no evidence, is that correct? It was the municipalities of -- let me just find them --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It was Rudo and Sipovo, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that's clear at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I might mention as a minor matter, it's not the Prosecution accept that is that's not necessarily an appropriate issue under Rule 98 bis but we wanted to make sure there was no misunderstanding about that because it sealed like an appropriate opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties do agree that no sufficient evidence under the Rule 98 bis test has been presented for these two municipalities, although whether this is something to strike out at this moment already is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. Right, for the reasons I expressed. I would say it slightly differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether an acquittal should follow on this basis or whether we should just keep that in the back of our minds for the future of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You wanted to raise an unrelated issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's simply this, Your Honour. The Prosecution would at the earliest possible stage like to know when, under Rule 65 bis(G), it can expect to receive a list of witnesses that the Defence intends to call so it can begin to prepare appropriately for the remainder of the case. I'm sorry, it's apparently 65 ter (G). I must have an old version. But I think the Court knows the provision to which I'm referring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the -- Mr. Josse, I take it that Mr. Stewart will take care of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, that's putting it, if I might say, succinctly accurately and helpfully from my point of view. It's a fundamental -- it's a fundamental matter so far as the Defence are concerned. Your Honour, speaking for myself and the rest of the Defence team, we are painfully aware of our obligations and what we need to do in regards to both the Rules and time in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber remembers well that just before the summer recess that we got a stormy weather forecast, although no direct warnings for the storm to arrive but it was indicated that something would come to the Chamber, but until now we have not received anything. So we would like to hear as soon as possible, at least the Prosecution would like to hear as soon as possible. If there are any problems, of course then it would be for the Chamber to hear about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: At the avoidance of any doubt, Your Honour, I can confidently say that regrettably, the matter will have to come back to the Chamber sooner rather than later. I realise the ball is in the Defence court. We are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we will adjourn and we will inform the parties as soon as possible when the oral decision will be delivered. It could be this week. There is even a fair chance that would be one of the following days. So the parties should be prepared to appear in court and to hear this decision to be delivered. If there is nothing else on the agenda at this moment, we will adjourn, as they say in good Latin, I think, sine die, that means without giving a date for our next hearing. We stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.36 p.m.
